findings.description: downloadSnapshot follows a 303 Location from Ring to any https URL and fetches it with the plain fetch. It carries no bearer token, redirect is 'error', and there is a timeout and a size cap, so impact is limited. A host allowlist, or at least a check that the host is not private or loopback, would harden this against a compromised or spoofed Ring response.
findings.title: Signed media URL is fetched from any https host without an allowlist

findings.description: /ring/webhook verifies only an HMAC over the body. A captured valid app_integration_removed event can be replayed to drop a later re-linked account's stored grant, because forget() removes the store record by account. The effect is a denial of service on a pilot, and the user would need to re-link.
findings.title: Webhook signature has no timestamp or replay protection

summary: Partial review. Controller verification (governance validation) passed with exit 0. I read only the Ring pilot dev code (bridge/dev/ring-pilot: snapshot.ts, links.ts, app.ts, client.ts), which holds the most recent changes. I did not open the connector, core, or contract sources under bridge/src (about 360 files), the specs, or the design documents, so nothing is said about them. In the files I read I found no blocking or major defects. Link confirmation, nonce replay protection, the one-time browser code, cookie flags, CSRF proof, the snapshot time-window bound and the JPEG size and shape checks all looked sound. Two minor observations follow.
